13:2: And Jesus -- Matthew 24:3 on the Olivet discourse: (See Scofield "Matthew 24:3").
13:8: sorrows -- birthpangs. Answering to the "seals." (Rev. 6.) Revelation 6:1-17. The death-agony of this age is the birth-agony of the next.
13:10: And -- Cf. Matthew 24:14 "Gospel of the Kingdom:" See note, Revelation 14:6 (See Scofield "Revelation 14:6").
13:13: end -- Not the end of the believer's life, but the end of the great tribulation. saved -- In the sense of Revelation 13:8; 20:4
13:14: when ye -- See "Beast." Daniel 7:8; Revelation 19:20 then let -- Cf. Luke 21:20-24. which is a prophecy fulfilled in the destruction of Jerusalem, A.D. 70, when the Christians escaped, and which foreshadowed the more terrible day here described. See "Great Tribulation."; Psalms 2:5; Revelation 7:14. (See Scofield "Psalms 2:5") See Scofield "Revelation 7:14".
13:19: affliction -- tribulation. Cf. Matthew 24:21 See "Tribulation."; Psalms 2:5; Revelation 7:14
13:26: Son of man -- Christ (Second Advent). Luke 12:35-40; Deuteronomy 30:3; Acts 1:9-11 (See Scofield "Matthew 8:20")
5:36: As soon as -- But Jesus, overhearing that word, said to the synagogue-ruler, Fear not, simply have faith. Cf. Luke 7:50
11:1: Bethphage -- Meaning, house of unripe figs, see Mark 11:12,20. probably so called after the fig tree was cursed.
11:13: leaves -- Fig trees which have retained their leaves through the winter usually have figs also. It was still too early for new leaves or fruit.
11:19: when even -- whenever, i.e. every day when evening came.
11:22: Have faith -- Have the faith of God; i.e. the faith which God gives. Cf. 1 Corinthians 12:9; Ephesians 2:8.
11:23: whosoever -- See, Matthew 17:20; Luke 11:1 (See Scofield "Luke 11:1"); Luke 17:6; John 14:13,14
11:26: if ye -- (See Scofield "Matthew 6:12"). Verse 26 is omitted from the best MSS.
4:22: For there is -- For nothing is hidden except unto manifestation, nor a secret thing done that shall not be exposed. Cf. Revelation 20:12; Romans 4:6; Hebrews 10:16,17
9:1: seen -- Cf. (See Scofield "Matthew 17:2") Also, 2 Peter 1:16-18 kingdom -- (See Scofield "Matthew 6:33")
9:27: Marg But -- But Jesus, grasping his hand, raised him, and he stood erect. Cf. Acts 3:7
9:29: This -- See, 1 Kings 18:42-45; Acts 13:2 The two best MSS. omit "and fasting." Cf. Matthew 17:21
9:31: The Son of man -- See, Mark 8:31 (See Scofield "Matthew 8:20")
9:39: miracle -- work of power upon my name, who will find it possible soon after to revile me.
12:1: vineyard -- Israel. Isaiah 5:1-7. Israel was not fruitless, but brought forth only wild grapes. Cf.; John 3:6; Hosea 10:1 contra, Hosea 14:8.
12:2: sent to -- Mark 12:2-5. the prophets and John the Baptist.
12:9: destroy -- Fulfilled in the destruction of Jerusalem, A.D. 70. Cf. Luke 21:20-24.
12:10: The stone -- See, Psalms 118:22,23 cf. (See Scofield "1 Peter 2:8")
12:24: said unto them -- See margin ref., (See Scofield "Matthew 22:29")
12:25: from the dead -- Lit. from amongst; cf., Philippians 3:11 Here it is the first resurrection. (See Scofield "1 Corinthians 15:52"). angels -- (See Scofield "Hebrews 1:4").
12:26: read in the book -- Jesus affirms the historic truth and inspiration of Ex. 3.
12:34: far -- i.e. not far in knowledge. He knew the very law which utterly condemns the best man -- its true office. Romans 3:19; 10:3-5; Galatians 3:10; Galatians 3:22-24.
12:35: son of -- i.e. David's Son only. Cf. Romans 1:3,4
12:36: For David -- Inspiration. (Jesus affirms the inspiration and Davidic authorship of Psa 110) Matthew 12:36; Luke 1:3; Exodus 4:15; Revelation 22:19 The Lord -- Jehovah. my Lord -- Adonai, Psalms 110:1.
8:15: leaven -- See note 4, (See Scofield "Matthew 13:33") Herod -- See margin ref., (See Scofield "Matthew 14:1")
8:23: And he took -- Our Lord's action here is most significant, Having abandoned Bethsaida to judgment Matthew 11:12-24. He would neither heal in that village, nor permit further testimony to be borne there Mark 8:26. The probation of Bethsaida as a community was ended, but He would still show mercy to individuals. Cf Revelation 3:20. Christ is outside the door of that church, but "If any man hear My voice," etc.
8:31: Son of man -- (See Scofield "Matthew 8:20") Also, Matthew 16:21-28; Mark 9:31; Luke 9:22-27; Luke 24:6
8:33: thou savourest -- i.e. thou art thinking man's thoughts, not the thoughts of God. Contra, Matthew 16:17
10:16: blessed them -- In Hebrew custom, a father's act. (Cf) Genesis 27:38 "He had no children that He might adopt all children."--Bengel.
10:18: Why callest -- Par., Believing Me to be but a human teacher, why callest thou Me "good," etc.
10:24: astonished -- Or, amazed, i.e. as Jews: knowing that temporal prosperity was, to the Jew as such, a token of divine favour. e.g. Deuteronomy 28:1-12.
10:25: eye of -- It has been thought the reference here was to a postern door set in a gate of Jerusalem.
10:28: Then Peter -- Cf. See note 2, Matthew 19:27-30 (See Scofield "Matthew 19:28")
10:45: life -- Or, soul. Cf. Isaiah 53:10,12 (Greek - ἀπόλλυμι," the soul or the essential life, not as commonly, "zoe," the active life).
10:51: Lord -- Gr. "Rabboni," my Master, a term of reverent love. Cf. John 20:16.
3:29: in danger -- is bound by an eternal sin.
15:16: the hall -- Or, the court which is the judgment-hall.
15:21: Rufus -- It is possible that this may be the same Rufus mentioned in Romans 16:13.
15:23: drink -- The stupefying drink usually given to those crucified.
15:24: And when -- See note for order of events at the crucifixion, (See Scofield "Matthew 27:33")
15:25: third hour -- Cf. John 19:14. John used the Roman, Mark the Hebrew, computation of time.
15:38: top to -- God rent it down; it was rent from the top. Christ having made atonement and glorified God, the way into the holiest was now made manifest. Cf. Hebrews 9:8,24; 10:19-22.
6:8: take nothing -- (See Scofield "Matthew 10:9") scrip -- provision-bag. purse -- belt.
6:14: Herod -- Son of the Herod of our Lord's nativity; also vs. Mark 1:16-18,20-22 See margin ref., Matthew 14:1 (See Scofield "Matthew 14:1")
6:20: and observed -- kept him safely, and, hearing him, did many things, hearing him gladly.
7:5: tradition -- i.e. the so-called "oral law" alleged to have been handed down from Moses; really a traditional interpretation of the written law. See margin ref., (See Scofield "Mark 7:7")
7:7: for doctrines -- as authoritative the precepts of men. Cf. v. Mark 7:5 See "Pharisees" Matthew 3:7 (See Scofield "Matthew 3:7") Cf.; Colossians 2:8,16,18,; Colossians 2:20,23
7:11: a gift -- Or, I have dedicated to God that which would relieve your need; Mark 7:12. No longer do you permit him to use it for his father or mother. Cf. Matthew 15:5,6
7:19: Because it entereth -- Because it does not enter into the heart of him, but into the bowels is passed -- purifying all the food.
7:28: And she -- She, however, answered, saying, True, Lord! and yet the little dogs under the table eat from the children's crumbs. Romans 11:24; Ephesians 2:11-22.
16:2: And very early -- For the order of events on the day of the resurrection, and for the order of our Lord's appearances after His resurrection, see, (See Scofield "Matthew 28:1") See Scofield "Matthew 28:9"
16:6: Ye seek -- Jesus ye seek -- the Nazarene, the crucified; He arose! He is not here! The tone is of triumph. Cf. Psalms 2:4.
16:9: Now when -- The passage from verse 9 to the end is not found in the two most ancient manuscripts, the Sinaitic and Vatican, and others have it with partial omissions and variations. But it is quoted by Irenaeus and Hippolytus in the second or third century. appeared -- (See Scofield "Matthew 28:9")
16:14: eleven -- A collective term, equivalent to "The Sanhedrin," "The Commons," not necessarily implying that eleven persons were present. See Luke 24:33; 1 Corinthians 15:5; Matthew 28:16 where "eleven disciples" implies a definite number of persons.
14:3: woman -- Mary of Bethany. head -- (See Scofield "Matthew 26:7")
14:17: And in -- For the order of events on the night of the last passover, (See Scofield "Matthew 26:20").
14:36: cup -- See note on the meaning of the cup. (See Scofield "Matthew 26:39").
14:38: flesh -- See, Romans 7:18,21-24 See note, Jude 1:23 (See Scofield "Jude 1:23").
14:45: Master -- Never once in the Gospel record does Judas Iscariot call Jesus "Lord." He was the first Arian amongst the professed followers of Jesus. No one can in reality say that Jesus is Lord, but by the Holy Ghost, 1 Corinthians 12:3 but it is possible to use the term as an empty formality without believing the Lordship of Christ; Matthew 7:21; 25:11,12.
14:53: And they led -- See note on order of events on the day of the crucifixion, (See Scofield "Matthew 26:57").
14:65: spit -- See, Isaiah 50:6 See note, Isaiah 52:14, (See Scofield "Isaiah 52:14") cf. Revelation 20:11
1:1: end of the world -- consummation of the age.
